key_insight: Extending antithetic sampling to equally spaced complex-circle points stabilizes Gaussian-smoothed high-order derivative estimates as the smoothing step approaches zero.
engineering_relevance: The estimator offers an alternative to costly high-order automatic differentiation, with demonstrated use in PINNs for high-order PDEs.
method: Estimate derivatives through Gaussian smoothing and Stein’s identity.
Replace reflection pairs with n equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane.
Under local analyticity and n at least the derivative order, obtain O(σ^n) bias and variance bounded as σ → 0.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate effectiveness in PINNs for polyharmonic and Cahn–Hilliard equations.
watch_item: The guarantees require local analyticity, and complex-valued function evaluations may complicate implementation.
paper_title: Variance Stable Gaussian Smoothing Estimator for Arbitrary High-order Derivatives
